compositions.title: Two dwellings and three birds
compositions.orientation: The old man is one of the builders. In his closing speech, ‘our’ includes all the builders.
compositions.text: Ðā gōdan męnn geworhton twā hofu. Ān hof wæs micel, and ān hof wæs lȳtel. Ðæt micle hof wæs māre ðonne ðæt lȳtle hof. Hīe sealdon ðæt micle hof ðǣm ealdan męnn. Hē hæfde ðrīe fuglas. Hē sealde his fuglum sǣd and wæter. Ðā fuglas lifdon on ðǣm miclan hofe. Se mann sægde: “Mīne fuglas sindon gōde. Ūre weorc is gōd.”
compositions.purpose: Connected nominal description and comparison with productive weak past verbs, ownership, counting, transfer, location and a present direct quotation. No new finite-verb system or subordinate-clause syntax.

teaching_examples.text: Gōd męte is on ðǣre eorðan.
teaching_examples.meaning: Good food is on the earth.
teaching_examples.purpose: Strong bare attributive adjective; prior locative phrase.

teaching_examples.text: Se gōda mann hæfð gōdne męte.
teaching_examples.meaning: The good man has good food.
teaching_examples.purpose: Weak determined subject versus strong bare accusative object adjective.
Weak attributive and strong predicate adjectives agree with one neuter noun.
Singular addressee; agreeing possessive chosen by possessor and inflected for the possessed object.
First-person plural possessor with masculine accusative plural agreement.
Near demonstrative and weak adjective with a neuter accusative object.

teaching_examples.text: Se mann is ieldra ðonne se fugol.
teaching_examples.meaning: The man is older than the bird.
teaching_examples.purpose: Umlaut comparative weak predicate with a parallel nominative standard.
Adverb modifying a previously taught weak action.
Dual personal subject with plural verb, distinct from cardinal plus ordinary plural noun.

teaching_examples.text: Ūre mann is on ðǣm ōðrum hofe.
teaching_examples.meaning: Our man is in the second dwelling.
teaching_examples.purpose: Agreeing possessive and exceptional strong ordinal after the article, within prior locative syntax.
